lint.description: Oxlint (no type-aware pass — tsc already covers types)

refs.description: Citation scanner — flags a bare, mislinked, or unglossed D#/C# tag

prose.description: Vale over the prose we own and can edit (docs, README, skills, src doc comments); voice anchored to docs/voice/
prose.note: One narrowing, deliberate: the path list replaces the adapter's bare `.`, because vale reads no .gitignore and skips no hidden directory, so `.` would sweep node_modules/, dist/, and the two record surfaces nothing may rewrite, CHANGELOG.md and .plumbbob/builds/. Every owned path is in the walk now. `skills/` joined last (2026-08-11), held out not by choice but by a parser: vale reads markdown frontmatter as YAML, an unquoted colon in a SKILL.md description raised E201, and one E201 abandons the entire run, so the path waited until all 13 descriptions were quoted; the 10 findings it brought were fixed the day it joined. The slot ran `optIn: true` until its first 59 findings were burned down by hand on 2026-08-11 (52 reworded; 7 were docs/generation-loss.md quoting the words these rules ban, now in code spans — a mention is not a use, and vale skips a code span the same way the refs scanner does). Nothing was baselined, and the slot now rides the default run and the fast turn gate like every other.

build.description: Publish build — `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` emits dist/, the artifact the npm tarball ships
build.note: Opt-in slot, turned on 2026-08-12. The `types` slot runs the base config, which is `noEmit`, so nothing in the default run ever exercised emit: `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` rewriting `.ts` specifiers to `.js`, `rootDir` pinning the dist/ layout the verbs resolve `../../` against. Only `prepack` and `pnpm eval:*` touched that path, which meant a broken artifact could stay green until publish. Runs at order 3 so a type error fails in `types` first, where the diagnostic is better. Costs about a second on the native compiler, so the turn gate keeps it.

test.description: Runs alone (order: single) — the suite saturates every core, so no other check shares its wave

spell.description: cspell over the owned prose and src/scripts code; project lexicon lives in cspell.json
spell.note: Turned back on 2026-08-26; the 2026-07 disable said only that cspell was not a dependency, and now it is. The walk mirrors the prose slot's idea of owned surfaces with two more exclusions: tests (fixture tokens are deliberate nonsense: typo probes like `drybrun`, regex stems like `approv`) and docs/voice (hand-owned; a finding there needs Rob's pen, and the gate must not block on a file only a human may edit). Citation names are scoped to docs/generation-loss.md by an override instead of riding the main word list. `language` is `en,en-GB` because the prose deliberately mixes both spellings. First 1430 findings burned down to zero the day it joined: all lexicon, no baselining, and no real typo found.

gate.note: vitest is ~53s of the ~56s full check — the per-turn Stop-hook gate skips it; `pnpm check` / checkpoint still run it
